column2: One should set up the pot, consecrated with the missile-mantra, cleansed with cow-water; cow's milk purified by the missile and consecrated with the "Prasada" mantra a hundred times.
One should put rice, millet and the like there, as follows: for the rite of one disciple, five handfuls of them;
afterwards, handful by handful one should increase for two and more in order. One should make the covering with the fire-mantra and the armor-atom.
In Shiva's fire, with the root-mantra, facing east, one should cook the porridge. When well cooked, on that hearth, having filled the ladle with ghee,
having given the heated pouring with Samhita mantras ending in svaha, having placed the pot on the mandala made with good darbha and the missile-atom,
having covered it with Om, having plastered its body with the heart-mantra, thus having obtained the cool pouring it becomes very cool.
One should perform with the Samhita mantras for the disciple, again and again; having offered on the seat of dharma and the rest west of the pit and mandala,
having offered the Sampata with the ladle, one should do the purification with the Samhita. Having taken the porridge once with that same mantra ending in vashat,
made nectar by the cow-mudra, one should lead it to the lord of the platform. With ghee portion; the share of the disciples; the share for the god and the fire;
the three with honey and ghee for the Stokapala and others one should make; with the heart-mantra ending in "namah" one should give rinsing water.
Having offered a hundred mantras with ghee one should give the full oblation by rule; the mandala east of the pit or in the middle between Shambhu and the pot;
having done the inner offering for the Rudras, the Mothers' hosts and the rest with the heart, one who has not received permission, having formed the notion of oneness even in Shiva,
I am endowed with omniscience and the rest, standing all around and above; a part of me is the place of union; I preside over the sacrifice —
I am Shiva, the egoistic one should leave the sacrificial pavilion. On a mandala made with the weapon-atom with darbha placed pointing east,
on the seat of Om the disciple, in a white upper cloth, bathed, facing north for liberation, and facing east for enjoyment,
having raised the body one should look east, from the feet to the crest for liberation, and in reverse for enjoyment,
with a gracious eye, revealing Shiva's abode; having sprinkled with the missile water, for the success of the mantra-water bath,
for ash-bathing, for the pacifying of obstacles and the breaking of sin, by the union of creation and destruction one should strike with ash of the missile-mantra.
Again, having sprinkled with missile water, for his completion, above the navel with the kusha tip one should touch uttering the missile-mantra;
one should touch thrice with those roots; below the navel for atonement of sin; and for the division of fetters one should touch with the arrow-atom.
In that body one should then place Shiva with limbs and seat. Of him, worshipped with flowers and the rest, the eyes with the eye-mantra or the heart-mantra,
having bound with a consecrated white cloth with fringe, having made him circumambulate and enter Shiva's right,
one should give a seat with cloth, offer according to caste. By the mudra of withdrawal, in the lotus of his heart one should place the Self in the form,
having restrained, in the purified body, having made the placement, one should worship him. On the head of the east-facing disciple with the root-mantra
Shiva's hand should be placed, giver of Rudra's lordship; the means of attaching to Shiva's service: the hand given with the Shiva-atom.
One should have a flower cast on Shiva, removing the worshipper; endowed with the mantras of that vessel's place, following the hosts of Shiva and the gods;
the teacher should make names in order for Brahmins and others, or as he wishes. Having had him bow to the pot and Vardhani near the fire,
one should seat him similarly on a seat on the right facing north. One should think of the Sushumna as emerging from the disciple's body,
dissolved in one's own seizing; having consecrated with the darbha root, having placed the darbha tip in the right palm of his hand,
its root on the Self's thigh and tip — on the banner of the peacock-bannered one; having gone to the disciple's heart with exhalation by the Shiva-atom,
having returned with inhalation into one's own heart, again with the Shiva-fire making such a joining of channels,

for his presence with the heart one should offer three oblations; for the steadiness of Shiva's hand one should offer a hundred with the root-mantra. Thus in the initiation of rule one becomes fit for worship of becoming.
For one whose bonds are loosened, the drawing up of power is, for the Self being a son of Rudra, called the impregnation.
The manifestation of the qualities of the three inner Selves here is held to be the male-engendering rite; knowledge by discrimination of illusion and Self is the parting-of-the-hair increase.
The acceptance from the purification of principles beginning with Shiva is held to be birth; the awakening as Shiva-hood is not held for one fit for Shiva-hood.
By the mudra of withdrawal one should take the Self, like a shining spark of fire, into one's own heart-lotus.
Then by the pot-practice one should utter the root-mantra; one should make equal control and then in the heart of the two Shivas.
By the order of abandoning the cause from Brahma onward, through exhalation-yoga, having led the Self up to Shiva, taking it with the rising mudra,
the one who knows the rule should place it with the mantra enclosed by the heart-mantra, by exhalation, in the pericarp of the disciple's heart-lotus.
Then the teacher should perform proper worship of Shiva and the fire; and bowing to himself, he should have the disciple hear the rules.
One should not blame the god nor the scriptures nor transgress the remnants and the like; worship of Shiva, fire and teacher is to be done as long as life lasts.
To children, fools, the old, women, those who indulge in pleasure, and the sick, one should give wealth according to ability; one capable should give all.
Having repeated in order the elements, matted hair, ash, staff and loincloth restraints with Ishana and the others or the heart-mantras,
having placed in vessels with Samhita mantras ending in svaha as before, having offered the prepared liquid, he should show it to the lord of the platform.
For protection having set it under the pot for a moment, having taken permission from Shiva, the teacher should give to the ascetic.
Thus in the special initiation of rule the disciple becomes especially fit for the knowledge of fire-oblation and the scriptures.
Having struck and taken, one should join it to the mouth-thread; one should offer with one's own seed-syllable three oblations for presence.
In knowledge: seven principles; twenty-one feet; six letters; one moving; twenty-five worlds;
three qualities and one; the object, cause of Rudra; having included within, in the excess, two accounts of the vital channels;
having taken the missile one should hold the foot of twenty-two; of worlds and of digits sixty, four qualities,
three and one of mantras, the object, the cause Hari; having included, in Pratishtha, with the white one the striking and the rest,
having done, the one on the navel-thread, having made present, one should worship with oblations. "Hrim" — of worlds a hundred and some, of feet twenty-eight;
of the seed-channel-winds, of both the two senses; of letters, principle and object each, the five qualities;
the cause lying in the mantra of the egg of Brahma, four of Shambaras; in Nivritti, in the yellow one, having included, one should strike.
At the beginning, at the end of that principle's portion, having placed on the thread one should worship; one should offer three oblations, having made present in the fire.
Thus having taken and joining to the thread of the digits from the disciple's body, in the initiation with seed, from the rule-conduct sacrifice,
for the protection of what begins the body, even from the fruit of mantra-accomplishment, for the sake of dharma such as sacrifices and gifts, the separate bond —
the subtle awakener of consciousness one should remember within the digits. By this same order then one should do the satisfying and the kindling,

with oblations with one's own mantra, three and three likewise. "Om Haum, to the bond of the digit beyond peace, svaha" and so on — the satisfying; "Om Ham Ham Ham, to the bond of the digit beyond peace, hum phat" and so on — the kindling; that thread for knowledge of pervasion in the five digit-places,
having taken up with saffron and ghee, one should worship Shiva with limbs there. Having pierced the bonds in order with the digit-mantras ending in hum phat,

and having entered within with those ending in "namah," one should make seizing and binding. "Om Hum Ham Haum Ham Hum phat — I seize and bind the digit beyond peace" and so on: the application of seizing and binding of the digits; the acceptance of the bonds and the rest, seizing, and binding again,
for the understanding of the whole activity regarding the person; having seated him, one should place that thread on the disciple's shoulder.
To remove the spread sin one should offer a hundred with the root-mantra. In a pair of bowls for a man, and for a woman on the belly,
having made the thread enclosed with the heart and the missile, one should worship with the heart. Having made the thread with Shiva with limbs, purified by Sampata,
one should place it under the pot and announce protection thus. Having given the disciple a flower in hand and worshipped the pot and the rest,
having had him bow, one should go outside to the middle of the sacrificial hall. Having made three circles, one should seat there the disciples — facing north for the seekers of liberation,
and facing east for enjoyment. In the first one should feed three mouthfuls of the five cow-products,
with hand joined with kusha, with intervals of worship; then in the third the porridge, the measure of three mouthfuls,
or the measure of eight mouthfuls, without touching with teeth; in a palasha leaf-cup for liberation, and in a pipal leaf for enjoyment,
having given the meal with the heart-mantra, he should have him rinse with pure water. Having made the tooth-stick with the heart, he should cast it in an auspicious place.
To remove faults of deficiency and the rest, with the root-mantra a hundred and eight, having done so, one should offer all works to the lord of the platform,
the dismissal of worship and the worship of Chandesha. Having removed the remnant, one should then offer the rest of the porridge in the fire.
Having worshipped and dismissed the pot and the guardians of the world, one should dismiss the hosts and the fire, if protected from outside,
outside, having briefly offered to the guardians of the world, having bathed with ash or pure water, he should enter the house.
Householders on a bed of darbha with heads east, well guarded; with the heart-mantra on a bed of good ash, ascetics with heads south;
with tuft bound, accompanied by weapons and seven boys, knowing, one should bathe the disciples and then go out again.
Om Hili Hili, to the trident-handed, svaha — having partaken of the five cow-products and porridge and taken the tooth-stick, having rinsed and meditated on Shiva, having gone to a purifying bed,
the teacher should lie down remembering the ritual of the initiation. Thus the rule for the preliminary dwelling at initiation is stated briefly.
